transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. It just feels like I'm running on empty constantly, and I can't seem to shake it.
Have you also been feeling down, sad, or uninterested in activities you used to enjoy, even when you're not physically tired?

Yes, absolutely. These past few weeks it's like this gray cloud has settled over me, leaving me feeling really hollow and hopeless even when I'm just at home. I’ve been canceling my usual fishing trips and completely neglecting my garden because I just can't bring myself to care enough to do any of it.
Have you lost interest in fishing and your garden because you feel too tired, or because those activities no longer bring you pleasure or satisfaction?

It’s really a combination of both. I’m so completely drained of energy that I usually just end up sitting on the couch, but I also just don't care about those hobbies anymore and they don't bring me any joy. Sometimes I'll just stare at the garden from the kitchen window because I can't bring myself to actually go out there.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F32", "R53"], but based on this conversation, R53 (which refers to general fatigue) is less likely as a standalone explanation because the patient exhibits not only persistent low energy but also core mood symptoms such as anhedonia (loss of pleasure in previously enjoyed activities), feelings of hopelessness, and emotional emptiness. These features strongly support a major depressive episode (F32) rather than non-specific fatigue. Therefore, F32 remains the primary candidate, while R53 is now considered insufficient to explain the full clinical picture.
